title: OleMiss vs UGA: tuition, size, location
summary: University of Mississippi (OleMiss) versus Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA). Also searched as UGA vs OleMiss. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Mississippi (OleMiss) and Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA) are both public institutions but differ significantly in size and location. OleMiss, located in University, Mississippi, has a much larger undergraduate enrollment of 21,473 students compared to UGA's 2,424 students in Americus, Georgia. Additionally, the in-state tuition at OleMiss is $9,772, which is higher than UGA's in-state tuition of $5,220. These differences highlight the contrast between a larger research university and a smaller regional institution.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: The University of Mississippi (OleMiss) and Georgia Southwestern State University are both public universities with distinct cost structures. OleMiss charges an in-state tuition of $9,772, which is notably higher than Georgia Southwestern State University's in-state tuition of $5,220. For out-of-state students, OleMiss tuition is $28,600, compared to $16,572 at Georgia Southwestern State University. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at OleMiss is $20,000, slightly above the $18,851 median debt reported by Georgia Southwestern State University. These figures illustrate the differences in tuition and financial outcomes between OleMiss and Georgia Southwestern State University.
